symptoms: None typically present at this stage.
medications: None required.
diet_suggestions: Incorporate complex carbohydrates and lean proteins.
lifestyle_changes: Engage in 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise per week.
preventive_measures: Avoid excessive consumption of processed sugars.

medications: Metformin may be considered by a physician for high-risk individuals.
diet_suggestions: Strictly avoid refined sugars and sweetened beverages.
Focus on the Mediterranean or DASH diet.
lifestyle_changes: Aim for 5-7% weight loss if overweight.
Increase daily physical activity (e.g., brisk walking).
preventive_measures: Reduce stress and ensure adequate sleep.
follow_up: Consult a primary care physician every 6 months.

medications: Oral hypoglycemic agents (e.g., Metformin, Sulfonylureas) as prescribed.
Insulin therapy
Advanced antidiabetic medications (GLP-1, SGLT2 inhibitors) as prescribed.
diet_suggestions: Consult a registered dietitian for a specialized plan.

medications: None required.

symptoms: Occasional shortness of breath during exertion
medications: Physician may consider low-dose statins if familial risk is high.
diet_suggestions: Switch to whole grains and plant-based fats.
preventive_measures: Monitor blood pressure weekly at home.

medications: Statins, Beta-blockers, or ACE inhibitors as prescribed by a cardiologist.
preventive_measures: Daily monitoring of blood pressure and weight.

medications: Intensive cardiovascular pharmacology (Anticoagulants, Diuretics, Nitrates) as prescribed.
diet_suggestions: Fluid restriction if heart failure is present.
Rigid diet adherence under clinical supervision.
lifestyle_changes: Complete rest and supervised minimal activity.
preventive_measures: Absolute avoidance of stress and physical exertion.
follow_up: Immediate hospitalization or very frequent cardiologist supervision.

medications: None required.
lifestyle_changes: Moderate alcohol consumption or complete avoidance.
preventive_measures: Avoid sharing needles or personal hygiene items.

medications: Avoid hepatotoxic medications (e.g., excess acetaminophen).
diet_suggestions: Avoid processed foods and high-fructose corn syrup.
lifestyle_changes: Weight loss if fatty liver is suspected.
preventive_measures: Review all supplements and medications with a doctor.

medications: Specific treatments for underlying cause (e.g., antivirals, immunosuppressants) as prescribed.
diet_suggestions: Low-sodium diet to prevent fluid retention.
Moderate to high protein from plant sources/dairy.
lifestyle_changes: Avoid raw seafood (due to bacteria risk).

recommended_tests: Continuous monitoring of LFTs, PT/INR, Kidney function
medications: Diuretics, Lactulose, Antibiotics as prescribed in clinical setting.
diet_suggestions: Strict dietary management via clinical nutritionist.
lifestyle_changes: Preparation for potential liver transplant evaluation.

medications: None required.
Blood pressure control medications if indicated.
diet_suggestions: Monitor protein intake (do not consume excess).
lifestyle_changes: Control blood pressure and blood sugar tightly.
preventive_measures: Consult a doctor before taking any supplements or pain relievers.

medications: ACE inhibitors/ARBs, Diuretics, Phosphate binders as prescribed.
diet_suggestions: Renal diet: restrict sodium, potassium, and phosphorus.
preventive_measures: Avoid contrast dyes for imaging unless necessary.
emergency_warnings: Shortness of breath due to fluid buildup

3.level: Critical Risk / End Stage Renal Disease
medications: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs), Iron supplements, active Vitamin D as prescribed.
diet_suggestions: Strict renal diet under a dietitian.
lifestyle_changes: Preparation for dialysis or kidney transplant.
follow_up: Immediate and ongoing nephrology care/dialysis center.

recommended_tests: TSH test every 5 years or during routine checkups
medications: None required.
diet_suggestions: Balanced iodine intake (e.g., iodized salt, seafood).
preventive_measures: Ensure adequate dietary selenium and zinc.

recommended_tests: Free T3, Free T4, Thyroid Antibodies (TPO, TGAb)
medications: Monitoring only; medication rarely required at this stage.
diet_suggestions: If hyperthyroid risk: avoid excessive dietary iodine. If hypothyroid: ensure adequate iodine.

recommended_tests: Frequent TSH and Free T4 monitoring
medications: Hypothyroidism: Levothyroxine. Hyperthyroidism: Antithyroid drugs (Methimazole) as prescribed.
diet_suggestions: Limit soy and goitrogens (e.g., raw cabbage, broccoli) if taking levothyroxine.
Take medication on an empty stomach.
lifestyle_changes: Adequate sleep and energy conservation if fatigued.
follow_up: Endocrinologist evaluation every 6-8 weeks until stable.

recommended_tests: Continuous clinical monitoring of thyroid hormones and vitals
medications: Intravenous thyroid hormones or beta-blockers/antithyroid drugs in ICU.
preventive_measures: Avoid stressors that trigger thyroid storm/myxedema coma.
emergency_warnings: Dangerously slow or fast heart rate

recommended_tests: Routine Pulmonary Function Tests (if exposed to occupational hazards)
medications: None required.
lifestyle_changes: Cardiovascular exercises to maintain lung capacity.

symptoms: Mild shortness of breath during exertion
medications: Short-acting bronchodilators (inhalers) as needed/prescribed.
diet_suggestions: Diet high in vitamins C and E.
preventive_measures: Avoid air pollution and respiratory irritants.
emergency_warnings: Wheezing that doesn't improve with inhaler

medications: Long-acting bronchodilators, inhaled corticosteroids, oral steroids during flare-ups as prescribed.
diet_suggestions: Frequent, small, nutrient-dense meals to prevent fatigue while eating.
Low-carbohydrate diet to reduce CO2 production.

symptoms: Inability to catch breath at rest
medications: Supplemental oxygen therapy.
Advanced systemic corticosteroids and antibiotics as prescribed.
diet_suggestions: Enteral nutrition if unable to eat.
preventive_measures: Avoid high altitudes and airplane travel without oxygen arrangements.
follow_up: Immediate hospitalization or intensive home nursing care.
emergency_warnings: Extreme difficulty breathing leading to panic

medications: None required.
diet_suggestions: Rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.

medications: Antihypertensives or statins if prescribed by physician.
follow_up: Consult a primary care physician every 6 months.

medications: Antiplatelets (Aspirin/Clopidogrel) or Anticoagulants as prescribed.
Intensive BP medication.
diet_suggestions: High potassium intake (unless contraindicated by kidney issues).
lifestyle_changes: Avoid heavy lifting or extreme exertion.
preventive_measures: Immediate reporting of any transient neurological symptoms.
follow_up: Consult a neurologist and cardiologist every 3 months.

medications: Emergency thrombolytics (tPA) if within window.
Advanced clinical management.
diet_suggestions: NPO (nothing by mouth) until swallowing evaluation in hospital.
emergency_warnings: Sudden severe headache with no known cause

medications: None required.
preventive_measures: Avoid excessive blood donation without adequate recovery.

medications: Over-the-counter multivitamin or mild iron supplements if recommended.
diet_suggestions: Incorporate iron-rich foods (spinach, red meat, lentils).
Pair iron with Vitamin C for better absorption.
lifestyle_changes: Avoid drinking tea/coffee with meals (inhibits iron absorption).
follow_up: Consult physician in 3-6 months to recheck CBC.
emergency_warnings: Shortness of breath with mild exertion

medications: Prescription iron supplements, Vitamin B12 injections, or folic acid as prescribed.
diet_suggestions: Avoid calcium supplements at the same time as iron.
lifestyle_changes: Avoid strenuous exercise until levels improve.

symptoms: Severe shortness of breath at rest
Chest pain (Angina) due to low oxygen delivery
recommended_tests: Type and Crossmatch for blood transfusion
medications: Intravenous (IV) iron.
Blood transfusions.
Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESAs) in clinical setting.
lifestyle_changes: Fall precautions due to extreme dizziness.
